# Contract: OccasionsRepository

Local-only Domain/Data boundary (see 001's `people_repository.md` for why this replaces a network API contract). All methods return `Either<Failure, T>`.

```dart
abstract class OccasionsRepository {
  /// Creates a new Occasion (FR-001). [idempotencyKey] is generated by the
  /// caller at "Save" time; a retried call with the same key returns the
  /// already-persisted occasion rather than creating a second one (FR-019).
  /// Rejects an empty [name] or empty [type].
  Future<Either<Failure, Occasion>> createOccasion({
    required String idempotencyKey,
    required String name,
    required DateTime date,
    required String type,
    String? notes,
  });

  /// Edits name/date/type/notes of an existing occasion (FR-012). Does NOT
  /// retroactively change countsTowardBalance on already-created
  /// participant contributions, even if [type] changes to/from
  /// 'condolence' (research.md Decision 3 — no silent balance changes).
  Future<Either<Failure, Occasion>> editOccasion({
    required String occasionId,
    required String name,
    required DateTime date,
    required String type,
    String? notes,
  });

  /// Archives an occasion (FR-014): hides it from the default list while
  /// preserving it, its attachments, and its participant contributions
  /// untouched (their balances keep counting).
  Future<Either<Failure, Unit>> archiveOccasion(String occasionId);

  /// Restores a previously archived occasion (FR-014).
  Future<Either<Failure, Unit>> restoreOccasion(String occasionId);

  /// Soft-deletes an occasion AND cascades to soft-delete every linked
  /// participant contribution in one DB transaction (FR-013, research.md
  /// Decision 5), appending a `deleted` TransactionAuditEntry per
  /// contribution via the existing 001 audit mechanism. The caller must
  /// have already shown the "N participants will be removed" confirmation
  /// (use [getOccasionDetail] to know N before calling this).
  Future<Either<Failure, Unit>> deleteOccasion(String occasionId);

  /// Records a participant's contribution: creates a MoneyTransaction with
  /// kind = occasionContribution linked to [occasionId] and [personId]
  /// (FR-003/FR-004/FR-005). [countsTowardBalance] defaults to false only
  /// when the parent occasion's type is 'condolence' and the caller does
  /// not explicitly override it (FR-018). Same idempotency contract as
  /// TransactionsRepository.addTransaction. Rejects amountMinorUnits <= 0.
  Future<Either<Failure, MoneyTransaction>> addParticipantContribution({
    required String idempotencyKey,
    required String occasionId,
    required String personId,
    required int amountMinorUnits,
    required TransactionDirection direction,
    bool? countsTowardBalance,
    String? note,
  });

  /// Edits an existing participant contribution's amount/direction/note
  /// (FR-010). Identical semantics whether called from the occasion
  /// detail screen or the person's own profile screen — both act on the
  /// same underlying MoneyTransaction row via
  /// TransactionsRepository.editTransaction, so there is exactly one
  /// place this write happens.
  Future<Either<Failure, MoneyTransaction>> editParticipantContribution({
    required String transactionId,
    required int amountMinorUnits,
    required TransactionDirection direction,
    String? note,
  });

  /// Removes a single participant contribution from an occasion (FR-011)
  /// after the caller has shown a confirmation. Soft-deletes the
  /// underlying MoneyTransaction (same mechanism as
  /// TransactionsRepository.deleteTransaction) so it disappears from both
  /// the occasion's participant list and the person's own history.
  Future<Either<Failure, Unit>> removeParticipantContribution(
    String transactionId,
  );

  /// Full detail for one occasion: the Occasion itself, its computed
  /// OccasionSummary (FR-007/FR-008), and its list of
  /// OccasionParticipantRow (FR-016), each participant's row carrying
  /// their own independently-computed overall PersonBalance.status
  /// (FR-009).
  Future<Either<Failure, OccasionDetail>> getOccasionDetail(
    String occasionId,
  );

  /// Occasions list, reverse-chronological by date by default (FR-015),
  /// filterable by name/type/date range and by archived state.
  Future<Either<Failure, List<Occasion>>> getOccasionsList({
    OccasionFilter? filter,
    bool includeArchived = false,
  });

  /// Attaches a photo already captured/picked by the presentation layer
  /// via AttachmentPickerService (core/media) and copied into the app's
  /// private storage directory (FR-017).
  Future<Either<Failure, OccasionAttachment>> addOccasionAttachment({
    required String occasionId,
    required String filePath,
  });

  /// Removes an attachment after the caller has shown a confirmation
  /// (FR-017).
  Future<Either<Failure, Unit>> removeOccasionAttachment(
    String attachmentId,
  );
}
```

**Failure modes**: `ValidationFailure` (empty name/type, non-positive amount), `NotFoundFailure` (unknown occasion/transaction/person id — surfaced as `OccasionNotFoundFailure`/`ParticipantNotFoundFailure` where the more specific message earns its keep), `CacheFailure` (local DB/file I/O error), `UnknownFailure`.

**Idempotency note**: `createOccasion` and `addParticipantContribution` are the two mutation methods that take an `idempotencyKey`, for the same reason established in 001 (`transactions_repository.md`): they are the only calls a rapid double-tap or process-restart retry could duplicate. `editOccasion`/`archiveOccasion`/`restoreOccasion`/`deleteOccasion`/`editParticipantContribution`/`removeParticipantContribution` all act on an already-identified id, so a retried call is naturally idempotent.

**Cross-feature note**: `addParticipantContribution`/`editParticipantContribution`/`removeParticipantContribution` are implemented by `OccasionsRepositoryImpl` delegating to the existing `TransactionsRepository` (extended per data-model.md) rather than writing to `MoneyTransactions` directly — this is what guarantees a contribution is the exact same row whether read from the occasion detail screen or the person's own profile screen (spec User Story 2, FR-005).
